title: Larry on patrol with a captured prisoner
description: Larry, in duck-hunter camouflage, crouches low in dense jungle looking back over his shoulder into the lens — an unposed frame taken by Captain Kennedy with his Nikon F. Close behind Larry crouches a prisoner the patrol had captured. In the account his son relayed on 2026-08-15 the man was a Pathet Lao, turned over to the CIA. In Larry's own words on 2026-09-12: "This guy was found in a hut by Sargent Lowry and they came out dragging him. He was tied up. No idea what he did. I heard he was Vietcong." A girlfriend was with him, and they told her to take off because the Vietnamese were coming; the prisoner was turned over to the Vietnamese, and the CIA were coming to get him from the ARVN. "You couldn't trust the ARVN's at all." The blurred face further back is a "striker" — a strike-force irregular; 70% of the strikers, Larry says, were enemy.
researchNotes: Relayed by Larry's son from Larry's dictation (2026-08-15 session; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0023-c18035445.json, -c18035515.json, and -c18035521.json). Unusual provenance: a photograph of Captain Kennedy's print (developed in Hawaii) — which both explains any generational quality loss and firmly places Kennedy on patrol with Larry, strengthening the tentative VN-0006 identification. 'Pasthic Lao' is read as Pathet Lao; a Pathet Lao prisoner taken near Tây Ninh (far from Laos) and handed to the CIA would be a remarkable, potentially documentable event — treated as a lead, now weakened (below). The '70% of strikers were enemy' assessment echoes documented CIDG infiltration concerns. Larry's own camera was a Canon Dial 35, bought at the Qui Nhơn PX (VN-0016 comment). 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0023-c18415971.json, transcribed): a fuller account in his own words that differs from the 2026-08-15 paraphrase on who the prisoner was — 'I heard he was Vietcong' against 'a pasthic Lao'. Both are hearsay on his own telling ('I heard'), both are kept, and neither is corrected; the later first-person account makes the Pathet Lao reading the weaker of the two (ledger #17, issue #97). New in it: Sgt. Lowry found the man in a hut, so Lowry was on this patrol or with it (data/people/sgt-lowry.json, issue #12), though Larry does not say Lowry is in the frame and he is not linked; the girlfriend sent away; and the hand-off in two stages, to the ARVN and then to the CIA. Location: 'to the left of Nui Ba Den' — a patrol in the country beside the mountain, not on it, so no place is set; the nui-ba-den record is the mountain and its camp.
